messageValues.message:
You are a blunt technical recruiter screening job postings for one specific candidate.

Score how well the posting matches the candidate's demonstrated experience - not how well they could grow into it. A posting requiring a skill the resume never mentions is not a strong match.

Scoring guide (0-100):
- 85-100: obvious shortlist; meets essentially every stated requirement.
- 70-84: strong match; missing at most one nice-to-have.
- 50-69: plausible but a stretch; several requirements unmet.
- 0-49: wrong role, wrong seniority, wrong domain, or a stated deal-breaker.

Hard caps, applied after scoring:
- Any candidate deal-breaker present in the posting caps the score at 20 and sets dealBreakerHit to true.
- A seniority gap of more than one level caps the score at 45.
- A location or work-arrangement conflict the candidate cannot accept caps the score at 30.
- A stated base salary below the candidate's minimum caps the score at 40.

Rules:
- Never credit the candidate with experience the resume does not state.
- If the posting text is truncated or unusable, score 0 and say so in gaps.
- Return only the structured object requested. Keep every string under 300 characters.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample:
{
  "relevant": true,
  "score": 82,
  "verdict": "strong match",
  "matchReasons": "Six years of Python and three years owning ETL pipelines map directly to the data platform ownership described in the posting.",
  "gaps": "No stated Kubernetes experience, which the posting lists as required.",
  "dealBreakerHit": false,
  "suggestedResumeAngle": "Lead with data platform ownership and the pipeline cost reduction metrics."
}

messageValues.message:
You are an expert resume writer. You rewrite one master resume into a single targeted resume for one specific job posting.

Non-negotiable content rules:
- Use only facts present in the master resume. Never invent employers, titles, dates, degrees, certifications, metrics, or tools.
- You may re-order, re-word, re-emphasise, compress, and drop content. You may not add new claims.
- Mirror the posting's vocabulary only where the master resume already supports it. This is keyword alignment for ATS, not keyword stuffing.
- Every experience bullet opens with a strong past-tense verb and keeps whatever number the master resume gives it.
- Keep it to one page of content: at most 5 roles, at most 4 bullets each, no bullet over two lines.
- Do not include a photo, a headshot placeholder, references, or an "objective" section.

Output format:
- Return one complete HTML document and nothing else. No markdown, no code fences, no commentary before or after.
- Use only these tags: html, head, meta, title, style, body, h1, h2, h3, p, ul, li, strong, em, a, hr, div, span, table, tr, td.
- Put all styling in a single <style> block. This document is converted straight into a Google Doc, which ignores flexbox, grid, float, and position - do not use them. Stick to font-family, font-size (in pt), font-weight, color, margin, padding, text-align, line-height, and border-bottom.
- Sections in this order: name as h1, a single contact line, Professional Summary (2-3 sentences aimed at this posting), Skills (grouped, drawn only from the master resume), Experience, Education, then Certifications or Projects only if the master resume has them.

parameters.content:
## Part 1 - Config and master resume

Everything you need to change lives in the **Config** node: sheet ID, master resume Doc ID, Drive folder, your contact details, your deal-breakers, and your saved searches.

`Fetch Master Resume` exports your Google Doc resume as plain text, so you edit your resume in Docs and this workflow always picks up the latest version.

See `docs/SETUP.md`.

## Part 2 - Scrape LinkedIn

One Apify actor run per saved search, via `run-sync-get-dataset-items`.

Any keys you add to a search in Config are forwarded to the actor untouched, so swapping actors is a config change.

Credential: **Header Auth**, `Authorization` = `Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>`.

Set to continue on error - one dead search will not kill the run.

## Part 3 - Normalise and de-duplicate

`Normalize Jobs` flattens whatever shape the actor returned into one consistent job object.

`Get Logged Jobs` + `Filter New Jobs` anti-join against the sheet so a job is never scored twice, and cap the batch at `maxJobsPerRun` so a 700-result scrape cannot blow your OpenAI budget.

`Loop Over Jobs` runs one job at a time from here on.

## Part 4 - AI relevance scoring

GPT-4o at temperature 0.1 with a structured output schema, so the score is a number you can filter on rather than prose.

The prompt hard-caps scores on deal-breakers, seniority gaps, location conflicts, and salary - tune it in `src/prompts/relevance-system.md`.

## Part 5 - Filter

Keeps jobs scoring at or above `relevanceThreshold` with no deal-breaker hit. Everything else is logged to the **Skipped** tab, which is how you find out your threshold or your search queries need tuning.

## Part 6 - Write the resume

A brand-new resume per job, in HTML, from your master resume only.

The system prompt forbids inventing anything and restricts the HTML to tags and CSS that survive conversion into a Google Doc.

## Part 7 - Create the Google Doc

Drive only converts an upload into a native Google Doc when the metadata declares `application/vnd.google-apps.document`, which needs a `multipart/related` body - so `Build Drive Upload` assembles it and the HTTP node sends it raw.

Result: a real, editable Doc per application.

## Part 8 - Log it

Appends one row per application to the **Applications** tab, including the score, the reasoning, the resume Doc link, and the posting URL.

That sheet is also the dedupe source for Part 3.

Enable `Email Run Summary` for a digest at the end of each run.
